archetype.name: Better Than Its Record (possession without finish)
archetype.definition: A Detroit team whose 5-on-5 share of chances and puck is its best in years, but which has been sunk by cold shooting, a bad penalty kill, poor goaltending from its busier starter and close-game losses.

report.headline: Detroit controls play better than in years and keeps losing anyway.
report.take:
On the standings page this looks like the same Red Wings who have finished outside the playoffs in every season on the sheet, only worse. They are 8-12-3, seventh in the Atlantic, 25th on the site, and on pace for 68 points after finishing on 92 last year. The process tells a different story. Detroit's 5-on-5 CF % of 51% ranks 8th, and its xGF % of 49.8% is the best of any season shown here, up from 46-48% for most of the last five years. They allow only 24.6 shots a game, 5th fewest in the league. That is a structurally sound team, not a bottom-eight one.

The losses come from three places, and the first is finishing. Detroit's skaters are shooting 6% in all situations, far below the league's 9.8%, and that is the main reason the offense ranks 30th at 2.61 goals a game despite holding the puck. The second is the penalty kill: at 70.8% it ranks 28th, and the 2024-25 team's 70.1% suggests this is a recurring weakness rather than a fluke. The third is in net. Daniil Tarasov has a .927 save %, +9.1 GSAx and two shutouts in 8 starts. John Gibson has started 14 games with a .862 save % and -7.7 GSAx. The team's overall goaltending looks roughly average only because those two lines cancel out.

Luck in close games is also against them. Pts vs Goal Diff sits at -2.7, 27th in the league, and the last ten games include a run of one-goal regulation losses to St. Louis, Vegas and Florida. Last season the same stat was +5.4, so the 92-point finish flattered that team the way this record undersells this one. November has been ugly: 2-7, scoring 2.11 a game against 2.93 in October, with a 2-8-0 last ten. A team out-attempting opponents at 5-on-5 does not usually keep shooting 6%.

The realistic view is a correction, not a rescue. The forwards grade D+ and the blueline C-, so this is not a talented roster waiting to break out. Its scoring should drift back toward normal, though, and Tarasov is giving it something close to elite goaltending. A 19-point start leaves a lot of ground to make up, but the team playing on the ice is a .500-ish club rather than the 68-point pace.

strengths.title: Puck control and shot suppression
strengths.body: Detroit owns 51% of 5-on-5 shot attempts, 8th in the league, and allows just 24.6 shots on goal a game, 5th fewest. Its xGF % of 49.8% tops every season on the sheet. This is structural, not a hot streak, and it has held through a losing November. It is the foundation that should keep results from staying this bad.

strengths.title: Tarasov is playing like a top goalie
strengths.body: Tarasov ranks 9th of 72 on the goalies tab, with a .927 save %, 1.98 GAA, +9.1 GSAx and two shutouts in 8 starts. In front of a team that limits shots, that is a winning formula. The sample is small and some fade is likely, but even a step back from this level would be a big upgrade on the alternative.

concerns.title: Gibson's starts are costing games
concerns.body: Gibson has taken the larger share of starts, 14, with a .862 save % and -7.7 GSAx, which ranks 60th of 72. On a team allowing so few shots, that save % turns tight games into losses. Unless the starts shift toward Tarasov, this drag continues, and it is the most fixable problem on the roster.

concerns.title: Shooting and special teams sink the scoreboard
concerns.body: Detroit's 6% shooting is far under the league's 9.8% and is the main reason it ranks 29th in goals a game. Some of that is a thin forward group graded D+, but this gap is mostly bad luck and should narrow. The penalty kill is a different matter. At 70.8%, 28th in the league, it has been this poor before, and the power play at 20% gives little back.

concerns.title: The hole is already deep
concerns.body: Even granting the bad luck, 19 points through 23 games puts Detroit on a 68-point pace. The last ten games went 2-8-0 with a -10 goal differential. Pts vs Goal Diff at -2.7 should even out, but regression only gets the team back to roughly break-even play, not a surge.

trend.note: October was a near-even 6-8 at 2.93 goals a game. November has gone 2-7 with scoring down to 2.11, and the 5-on-5 numbers have not collapsed along with the results.

weekAhead.headline: Two bottom-feeders and an overachiever: a real chance to stop the slide.
weekAhead.body:
The schedule finally eases. Vancouver comes to Detroit as the site's 32nd-ranked team: 6-19-1, last in Goal Diff / GP, xGF % of 39.2%, a 61.2% penalty kill and goaltending 32nd in GSAx. For a team that has been starved for goals, it is the ideal opponent. Columbus on the road is 26th on the site and has the league's lowest-scoring offense, though it plays a similar possession game (51% CF %) and holds opposing forwards in check.

Nashville closes the week at home and is the only test. Its 12-6-5 record is built on A- goaltending and a 2nd-ranked penalty kill rather than control of play: its CF % of 47% ranks 25th, and its Pts vs Goal Diff of +2.8 is the mirror image of Detroit's. Anything less than two wins from the first two games would be a missed opportunity.

keyMatchups.title: Vancouver's leaky net and kill
keyMatchups.body: The Canucks save .866 in all situations, 31st, and kill only 61.2% of penalties. Their defense also gives up the most to wingers relative to expectation of almost any team. Detroit's cold shooters are facing the goaltending most likely to break the slump.

keyMatchups.title: Columbus: two shot-suppressing teams
keyMatchups.body: Columbus ranks last in scoring and holds opposing forwards to the 4th-lowest output against expectation. Points against them have come disproportionately from defensemen. Expect a low-event game where Detroit's blueline has to activate.

keyMatchups.title: Nashville's goalie against Detroit's possession
keyMatchups.body: Detroit should hold the puck against a 25th-ranked CF % team. The Predators' goaltending grades A-, though, and their penalty kill is 89.1%, so a Detroit power play at 20% is unlikely to bail it out. This game is decided at 5-on-5.

weekAhead.watch: Who starts in goal: whether Tarasov, with his .927 save %, takes the bulk of this week's starts over Gibson.

restOfSeason.body:
Detroit's underlying profile is good enough to play around .500 hockey from here. That means puck control, shot suppression and a goalie posting +9.1 GSAx. The 6% shooting and the -2.7 Pts vs Goal Diff are the parts most likely to regress in its favor. The 70.8% penalty kill and a forward group graded D+ are real, and they cap the upside. Gibson's numbers are the swing: if he settles to even average, or Tarasov takes over the net, the team's results should catch up to its 5-on-5 play.

The early deficit is the problem. A team with 19 points after 23 games needs a strong close just to reach the mid-80s that have not been enough in recent seasons. A finish in the low-to-mid 70s in points, with the goal differential improving steadily, is the likeliest outcome. Expect something like 74 points: better than the 68-point pace, short of the playoff line.

confidence.note: 23 games is a modest sample, but the gap between process and results is wide and consistent. The forward roster data is thin.
